aions_core/server/cbms_outline.py.why: Its subject is the chunk files themselves - their ids, sizes, access counts and active-versus-parked tier - so it is bookkeeping over the pile rather than ranking passages to answer a question.

control_plane/agents/agent_registry.py.why: What it discovers are helper roles with allowed-skill lists and risk caps, not the runnable actions themselves, so it belongs with roles rather than with the skills library.

control_plane/blends/__init__.py.why: It marks the package holding the mistake-and-lesson tooling, so it sits with long-term self-improvement rather than with any answer-grading area.

control_plane/blends/write_conclusion.py.why: It finishes the write-up of a past mistake into a lesson, and only afterwards optionally emits a chunk file, so the lesson-drawing is the point and the chunk is a by-product.

control_plane/llm_adapter.py.why: It assembles the prompt and calls a locally hosted model, which is the calling machinery, not the tone-shaping of a finished reply.

control_plane/skills/forge_linux_verify..why: It gates a brand-new ability into the live library by schema, compile and sandbox trial, which is the approval pipeline rather than the everyday running of approved skills.

control_plane/skills/goal_planner.py.why: It chooses and chains entries from the skill catalogue and replays learned recipes, unlike the control-plane planner which numbers steps and picks a worker machine.

control_plane/skills/papiery.py.why: The records it keeps are the owner's own tasks with deadlines, priorities and tags, not knowledge chunks the system learned.

control_plane/skills/recipes.py.why: It remembers known-good skill chains so a repeat request replays them, which is the library's reuse memory rather than a lesson drawn from a mistake.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/__init_.why: It only decides transport and port and boots the tool service, so it is the start-up plumbing rather than any of the abilities that service exposes.

scripts/test_node_registry.py.why: It exercises the roll of worker machines and the plan-to-execution path, not the health of a live installation.

scripts/turbo_scanner.py.why: It surveys source files for duplicates, hubs and import links across the drives, which is a stocktake of code rather than a check on running services.

scripts/vault/_core.py.why: It locks credentials into a per-account encrypted store, which is credential safekeeping, not a rule about which actions an agent may take.

scripts/vault/open_secret.py.why: It takes a sealed credential back out to a tightly permissioned file, the other half of the same encrypted store rather than any permission gate.

server/models.py.why: It states the request and reply shapes for the similarity store's web service - sessions, batches, scored hits - rather than defining anything about plain chunk files.

aions_core/claude_aions_bridge.py.why: Its job is deciding whether the retrieved material suffices or a bigger model must be asked, which the model-running area explicitly excludes.

aions_core/server/refgraph.py.why: It tracks which stored pieces point at which and flags broken or archived-dependency links, which is upkeep of the pile, not searching it for an answer.

aions_core/tools/analyze_csv.py.why: It reads a whole-disk scan listing to report where chunk folders and critical files sit, so it is a survey of the drives rather than maintenance of the chunk store itself.

aions_core/unified_core.py.why: It is the top layer that boots every component, tolerates the ones that fail and routes a query through them, rather than being any one of those components.

control_plane/agents/agent_runner.py.why: Its whole logic is narrowing a role to its allowed actions and refusing anything above its risk ceiling, unlike the plain executor that just runs a planned step.

control_plane/llm/server_client.py.why: It is the thin talker to a locally hosted model server that stays loaded in memory, and it reports failure rather than judging whether the model was needed.

control_plane/operator/mouth.py.why: It attaches a plain-language note to an incident the self-repair loop already decided on, so it belongs to live health rather than to the tone of a user-facing reply.

control_plane/policy.py.why: It is the plain allow-list and dangerous-command block-list consulted before anything runs, not a judgement about whether an answer is trustworthy.

control_plane/skills/semantic_search.py.why: What it hunts for is the right reusable action for a plainly worded request, not the passage that answers a user's question.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/test_se.why: It exists only to prove the tool-server protocol itself starts and replies, not to demonstrate the system doing a real job.

scripts/aions_tray.py.why: It is the taskbar control for the desktop application - start, stop, open logs - rather than a sweep that measures whether services are healthy.

scripts/demo_secretary.py.why: It is a runnable showcase of the skill engine end to end, calling into the library rather than being part of it.

scripts/proof_provenance.py.why: It confirms what actually landed in the similarity store after a write, which is the after-the-fact check on that database rather than a judgement of answer quality.

server/store_api.py.why: It mirrors the similarity store's own interface over the network so callers cannot tell local from remote, making it part of that database's service layer.
